provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 text layer damages 4 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: quesumus domine -> qusesumus d mine; respice -> r spice; carnalibus -> cara libus; cessare concede -> cessdre conc le per dominum alicc orationes; 1922 Mame text layer damages 4 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): populum -> opulum; quesumus domine -> mus demine; precipis -> prcipis; noxiis -> noxils; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 104, artifact PDF p. 218; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 29282 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Populum tuum, quaesumus, Domine, propitius respice: et, quos ab escis
carnalibus praecipis abstinere, a noxiis quoque vitiis cessare concede. Per
Dominum nostrum.

refused.catholic-public-domain-version: Esth 13:8 is recorded as not carried by this edition: this edition prints Esther in the Septuagint arrangement and in fifteen chapters, so no Vulgate chapter or verse number addresses the matter it names: its 1:1 is the Vulgate's 11:2, its 3:1 is the Vulgate's 1:1, and its 13:9 is part of the king's letter and not Mardochai's prayer

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Hostias, Domine, quas tibi offerimus, propitius respice: et per haec sancta
commercia, vincula peccatorum nostrorum absolve. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum
Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.
